paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Jesus walks up to a tax collector at his booth and says, "Follow Me," and Levi gets up and follows Him (Luke 5:27-28). Then the Pharisees, a group of religious leaders, and their scribes ask Jesus' disciples, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?" and Jesus answers, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick" (Luke 5:30-31). He says He has come to call sinners to repentance (Luke 5:32), so Jesus came for people who know they need Him and calls them to turn back, and nobody has to clean up first.

Now the second half, and this one is a little sneaky. Jesus says the bridegroom's guests can't fast while He is with them, and a time will come when He is taken from them (Luke 5:34-35). Then comes the parable: a new patch on an old garment, new wine in old wineskins (Luke 5:36-38). What Jesus brings doesn't get squeezed into the old way of doing things. It needs room to be what it is, and I know a thing or two about being squeezed into a small space, because I spent years in a junk drawer.

And look at that last line, because it's the warning. Jesus says that after drinking old wine, no one wants new, for he says, "The old is better" (Luke 5:39). It's easy to get comfortable and call it wisdom. So ask yourself, baker: is there a spot where you've been saying "the old is better," when Jesus is standing there saying, "Follow Me"?
